claims.text: The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy contains approximately 20 at.% each of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr.
The plastic strain and toughness of WTaTiVZr under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service are governed by its combination of refractory elements.
The refractory-element combination alters dislocation density in WTaTiVZr relative to commercially used pure tungsten.
The refractory-element combination alters grain-boundary structure in WTaTiVZr relative to commercially used pure tungsten.
The altered dislocation density provides additional pathways for dislocation glide.
The altered grain-boundary structure provides additional pathways for grain-boundary sliding.
Additional dislocation glide and grain-boundary sliding enhance the alloy's plastic strain and toughness.
These deformation pathways improve resistance to deformation and cracking under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than pure tungsten under the stated service conditions.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater toughness than pure tungsten under the stated service conditions.
The proposed mechanism is intended to apply above 1000°C in a plasma-radiation environment.
The hypothesis may not apply at lower temperatures or under different radiation conditions.

A controlled comparison using tensile testing, scanning electron microscopy, and transmission electron microscopy can measure plastic strain, toughness, dislocation density, and grain-boundary structure in WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten.
Failure of WTaTiVZr to improve both plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten would falsify the predicted outcome.
Absence of a significant difference in dislocation density or grain-boundary structure relative to pure tungsten would count against the proposed mediator.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says easier glide and grain-boundary sliding enhance plastic strain while also improving resistance to deformation. Greater deformability and greater resistance to deformation are not necessarily incompatible, but the hypothesis does not distinguish plastic accommodation from strength, leaving the asserted effects conceptually unresolved.
